column1: # Mutation-testing baselines — a RATCHET, not a to-do list, and NOT a claim that the
# remaining survivors are harmless.
# SPANS IS AT ITS FLOOR — 10, and all ten are EQUIVALENT MUTANTS (measured 2026-08-13).
# Do not spend another pass on `spans`. Tests were written for all ten, the file was
# registered in MODULE_TESTS[spans], coverage reached 98%, and the count did not move —
# because none of the ten can change observable behaviour:
#   * a corrupted `style` default or fallback is normalised back, and `_placeholder`
#     falls through to the label form for ANY unrecognised value (incl. None);
#   * `not text or not spans` -> `and` reaches the same answer via `if not applied`;
#   * `char_start > cursor` -> `>=` and `cursor < n` -> `<=` append the empty string;
#   * both `build_word_offsets` mutants sit on the FIRST `idx < 0` guard, where the
#     fallback `text.find(token)` re-finds the same index.
# Full reasoning: backend/tests/redaction/test_apply_redactions_mutants.py.
# Lowering this baseline requires changing spans.py, not adding tests.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# "Kill every surviving mutant" is not a finishable goal on this codebase: an AST census of
# lockout's 149 survivors (regenerate mutmut's mutants from the source, map each survivor back
# to the line it edits, ask whether that line is inside a logging call) finds 58 that edit a log
# string and 8 that flip a condition guarding only a log call. No caller can observe those, and
# asserting on log text creates tests that break on every reword. Without a bounded definition
# of done, each pass closes a few real gaps and leaves a large residue — which reads as no
# progress.
# So the gate is: the survivor count for a module may go DOWN, never UP. A new untested
# predicate raises it and fails `--check-baseline`. That is the same shape as the coverage
# `fail_under` ratchet in backend/pyproject.toml, and for the same reason.
# READ THE NUMBERS AS A CEILING, NOT AS AN ALL-CLEAR. The same census over all six modules puts
# 167 of the 636 survivors (26%) in the log-string / log-branch bucket. The other 461 are
# ordinary predicates, comparisons, assignments and default arguments — code a caller CAN
# observe, and each one is a line the suite executes without checking. The counts below bound
# the residue; they do not excuse it.
# This file is READ by `./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --check-baseline`. It is not
# documentation: a checked-in table nothing reads goes stale, which is exactly how
# `expected-schemas.tsv` died. It went stale here anyway — two of the notes below described
# measurements nobody had made (see spans and lockout) — so every note now states what was
# measured and how.
# ⚠️ ALL SIX ROWS CURRENTLY AWAIT RE-MEASUREMENT. `--check-baseline` reports them NOT MEASURED
# (exit 4), because a run log is only admissible with the completion + source-binding evidence
# a run now writes beside it (<key>.meta), and the 2026-08-12 logs predate that. The numbers
# below are the last recorded LEVEL, not a verified state. Two of them are independently known
# to be stale: regenerating mutants from today's source produces 10 mutants security.log names
# but the current app/core/security.py cannot make (c0c462aa changed it), and security's own
# note already said its verify_token gap closed after the run.
# HOW TO UPDATE
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --clean            # stale cached verdicts are the #1 trap
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --module <name>
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --check-baseline <name>
# Lower the number when you have added tests. NEVER raise it to make a run pass — that is the
# one move this file exists to prevent. Raising it needs a reason in the commit message.
# COVERAGE is recorded alongside because a survivor count is meaningless without it: a module
# whose selected tests execute 56% of it reports survivors that measure test SELECTION, not
# test strength. That happened to `lockout` and produced 41 false findings in `dependencies`.
# module<TAB>max_survivors<TAB>min_coverage_pct<TAB>measured_on<TAB>note

column5: 10 survivors of 206, and ALL TEN ARE EQUIVALENT (verified 2026-08-13 by writing tests for every one: registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 97%->98%, count unmoved). Corrects the previous note, which called 5 of them 'operator flips in live predicates' — those 5 are equivalent too: `or`->`and` reaches the same answer via `if not applied`; `char_start > cursor`->`>=` and `cursor < n`->`<=` append the empty string; and BOTH `idx < 0` mutants sit on the FIRST guard, where the fallback `text.find(token)` re-finds the same index. This is a FLOOR: lowering it needs a change to spans.py, not more tests. Reasoning: tests/redaction/test_apply_redactions_mutants.py.

column1: dependencies
column5: 186 -> 175, and the 186 was a REGRESSION off 180 this row was never raised to accept. 6 of the 186 came from wave 2/3: 4 from `_get_client_info`'s new `request is None` branch (the BRANCH was killed, its return VALUE was not — a test now pins the ("unknown","unknown") placeholder, which the audit index groups by) and 2 from `accepted_algorithms(None)`, which are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT and are not killable from a test: `core.security.signing_algorithm` does `del token_type` and returns `settings.JWT_ALGORITHM`, so `accepted_algorithms(None)` returns the identical list (measured: ['HS256','HS512'] both ways). 11 killed in total, each control-verified: the 4 above plus 7 in `_banner_requirement` — 6 of which needed a REAL session, because `test_banner_acknowledgment.py`'s fake answers every `filter()` with the same rows, so a mangled `login_banner_*` key, a dropped filter and the wrong model were all invisible while Postgres returns nothing and the gate silently falls back to .env; plus the .env fallback itself, which nothing asserted ENABLES the gate (every existing case asserted it does not engage). Coverage 93 -> 94.

column1: password_policy
column5: 86 -> 46 of 292, and 46 is a FLOOR unless password_policy.py itself changes: every one of the 46 was classified from its diff and the classification then MEASURED. 40 killed by the new tests/unit/test_password_policy_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 94% -> 100%), and the 46 left are EXACTLY the 43 noise + 3 equivalent predicted before the run, id for id. The 43 noise all sit in check_password_history's degradation report — the logger.warning/logger.exception strings, the 7 fragments of the operator %s message, and the checked/unverifiable counters, which feed only that message's %d slots (the critical-vs-error LEVEL split, which is what an alert keys off, is already pinned by test_password_policy_controls.py). The 3 equivalent: the wrapper's new_password_hash="" -> None/"XXXX" (the method never reads that parameter) and history_count <= 0 -> < 0 (the two disagree only at 0, where the mutant falls through to password_history[:0], an empty slice, and returns True anyway). The 40 kills were each control-verified BEFORE the run by monkeypatching the individual mutant function from the gitignored mutants/ copy and watching a test fail — with the unmutated __mutmut_orig, the 3 equivalents and 3 noise mutants as negative controls, all of which correctly reported SURVIVED (the first version of that harness reported KILLED for everything, including orig, because a stray /tmp/token.py shadowed the stdlib). Biggest real gaps closed: the module-level wrappers (get_days_until_expiration/is_password_expired/password_expiry_cutoff) were never called with an explicit current_time, so dropping the caller's clock and answering "as of now" was invisible; is_password_expired's <= cutoff boundary and its return True for a NULL password_changed_at; every tzinfo normalisation in expiry_cutoff/is_password_expired/get_days_until_expiration (3 mutants each, all killed at once by a naive input, which raises TypeError); max_age_days <= 0 -> <= 1 and history_count <= 0 -> <= 1, each turning the smallest configurable nonzero value into a second off switch; and the uppercase/lowercase/digit error strings, which are response-body text the SPA renders, not log output.
